subject: Dedicated slice contention: EdgeMed vs Astral — proposed tie-break and temporary slices
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: competing Dedicated requests for Oct 1 start — EdgeMed vs Astral

Vivek / Olga —

Heads-up: both EdgeMed (customer-facing health AI) and Astral Labs (logistics AI) signed commitments that would require dedicated GPU reservations starting Oct 1. Combined requested capacity exceeds the uncommitted pool by ~28 GPUs for their initial tranche. EdgeMed has a signed PO (see attached EDG-commit-summary.pdf) and legal already countersigned; Astral has DA in negotiation but is projected to convert this week.

Quick context: EdgeMed is asking for a 40-GPU reserved lane (8xA100 equivalents) for a 12-month term with strict SLOs; Astral asked for a 32-GPU tranche with a higher burst profile. Both are high-priority but for different reasons (EdgeMed: enterprise healthcare vertical + compliance; Astral: strategic partner, potential volume expansion Q1).

Can we align on a temporary allocation solution + final tie-break rules so sales/ops can communicate to both parties? We need a decision by EOD tomorrow to avoid cascading procurement delays.

Proposed quick options (informal):
- Option A: Honor signed PO (EdgeMed) for initial tranche; offer Astral a 70% immediate slice + ramp plan and priority for next replenishment.
- Option B: Split available uncommitted pool 50/50 for first 30 days and schedule a joint review with CS/Revenue to determine long-term sizing.
- Option C: Short-term transient scheduling: time-windowed reservations (EdgeMed peak 00:00-12:00 PST; Astral 12:00-24:00 PST) and shared KV cache rules.

Olga — your input on the operational feasibility of C (time-windowed reservations and prefix caching carve-outs) would be helpful. Vivek / Laura — which option respects sales commitments and does least commercial damage?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: EDG-commit-summary.pdf (summary of signed PO, committed tokens, SLOs)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: competing Dedicated requests for Oct 1 start — EdgeMed vs Astral

Ben —

Operational feasibility notes after quick check with Fleet and Runtime teams:
- Time-windowed reservations (Option C) are technically feasible for a 30-day pilot but will require temporary routing policies + KV cache partitioning. There is ~2-3 day lead time to implement safe fallbacks and traffic shaping.
- Splitting GPUs 50/50 (Option B) is simplest to deliver immediately but results in both parties receiving lower throughput and may violate EdgeMed's signed SLOs unless we compensate via credits.
- Honoring the signed PO (Option A) is straightforward commercially but leaves Astral under-served and might jeopardize partner momentum.

Risk assessment: EdgeMed's legal-signed PO has an explicit start date; failing to meet that could require credits or escalation to director level. Astral's volume profile shows they hit 85% of requested capacity within their first week in our mid-stage sim — meaning Astral will press for more capacity quickly.

Operational recommendation: implement Option C for the first 30 days (time-windowed carve-outs) while prioritizing EdgeMed's compliance needs during their peak window. During that month we execute a gating review with CS and Sales to re-evaluate long-term tranching. This reduces immediate SLA risk and buys 30 days to either expand capacity or re-negotiate Astral's ramp.

I can schedule the deployment with infra tomorrow but need commercial confirmation to proceed (credits/compensation framework for EdgeMed if we choose shared split).

Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Capacity & Fleet Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: allocation-temporary-slice-plan.xlsx (top-level plan; will share full sheet in Drive)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: competing Dedicated requests for Oct 1 start — EdgeMed vs Astral

Thanks, Ben / Olga.

Agree with Olga's balanced approach. My commercial constraints: EdgeMed's PO references a firm start date and a penalty clause for missed SLO in the first 60 days — we should avoid triggering that. Astral is strategic, but their contract is not fully executed. Given that, I authorize Option C (30-day time-windowed carve) with the following caveats:

- We honor EdgeMed's primary time-window where they must have guaranteed capacity (documented in EDG-commit-summary).
- We commit to a review call on Day 21 to confirm either: additional capacity procurement or a formalized long-term split.
- Sales to offer Astral a temporary 25% ramp discount on their first invoice to acknowledge the interim arrangement.

Ben — please confirm you can offer the 25% ramp concession and communicate the temporary nature and Day-21 review. Olga — please proceed with the deployment plan and confirm timelines. Laura — loop in CS for the Day-21 ops review and customer comms.

I'll be on standby to escalate to SVP if either customer pushes.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Gomez <maya.gomez@edgemed.com>, Holly Park <procurement@edgemed.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-19T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: RE: EdgeMed PO and Oct 1 start — temporary scheduling plan

Maya / Holly —

Thanks again for returning the signed PO. We want to confirm next steps to make the Oct 1 start reliable. Redwood will implement a short-term allocation plan to guarantee EdgeMed's primary capacity window while we finalize longer-term tranching. Key points:
- Start date: Oct 1 (no change)
- Guaranteed tranche: 40-GPU equivalent during 00:00-12:00 PST daily for first 30 days
- Failover: if we detect sustained overload we will automatically spill to compatible hosted instances and notify you immediately
- Credits: if we miss guaranteed throughput attributable to Redwood misconfiguration, EdgeMed is eligible for service credits per the signed contract

We will hold a Day-21 review (Oct 21) with your technical and procurement teams to finalize capacity for Nov onward. Olga will send the technical configuration and contact for onboarding by EOB today.

If that aligns, please reply with a quick OK so we can proceed.

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@astrallabs.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Astral Sales <sales@astrallabs.io>
Date: 2027-09-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity requests / Astral ramp

Ben / Vivek —

Appreciate the transparency. Astral can accept a temporary scheduling carve if we get firm commitments on two items:
1) A guaranteed ramp timeline to reach 100% of requested tranche by Nov 1 if capacity allows (not negotiable for our internal roadmap).
2) A credit structure for the limited initial window and a clause to escalate priority if we demonstrate production load >80% for 4 consecutive days.

If Redwood can put those commitments in writing (email confirmation + appendix to the MSA), Astral will sign the DA this week and accept the Oct 1 transient arrangement. That will preserve their partner momentum.

Please confirm and share the DA redline contact.

Thanks,
Liam Chen
Head of Infrastructure
Astral Labs
